A faithful, open .docx editor — running a native Rust core in your browser

BetterOffice is a client-side editor for .docx documents with an unusual architecture: parsing, editing, text shaping, and page layout all run in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly. Your file never leaves your device — there is no upload and no server round trip — yet every page is laid out with the fidelity of a desktop word processor.

The page you are reading is not HTML pretending to be a document. A native layout renderer measured every line and painted this page onto a canvas — the same way a desktop word processor would. Try selecting text, changing a heading, or editing a table cell: the engine reflows the page live.
A native engine, compiled to WebAssembly

Opening a file runs the whole pipeline in Rust: the parser reads the OOXML into a typed document model, the text engine shapes every run with real font bytes, the paginator breaks lines into pages, and the result is emitted as a display list that the browser simply replays onto canvas. The DOM is never asked to lay out a document — fidelity does not depend on the browser.

The Rust text shaper keeps character formatting intact: bold, italic, underline, a colored run, and even a highlighted run all survive the round trip.

renderDocx:
Welcome to BetterOffice

A faithful, open .docx editor — running a native Rust engine in your browser

BetterOffice is a client-side editor for .docx documents with an unusual architecture: parsing, editing, text shaping, and page layout all run in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly. Your file never leaves your device — there is no upload and no server round trip — yet every page is laid out with the fidelity of a desktop word processor.

The page you are reading is not HTML pretending to be a document. A native layout engine measured every line and painted this page onto a canvas — the same way a desktop word processor would. Try selecting text, changing a heading, or editing a table cell: the engine reflows the page live.

# A native engine, compiled to WebAssembly

Opening a file runs the whole pipeline in Rust: the parser reads the OOXML into a typed document model, the text engine shapes every run with real font bytes, the paginator breaks lines into pages, and the result is emitted as a display list that the browser simply replays onto canvas. The DOM is never asked to lay out a document — fidelity does not depend on the browser.

## Character formatting

The Rust text shaper keeps character formatting intact: **bold**, *italic*, underline, a colored run, and even a highlighted run all survive the round trip.

## What runs in Rust

The engine owns the document end to end:

- An OOXML parser and serializer that round-trip .docx files byte-faithfully
- Text shaping and measurement with real font bytes — never the browser
- Pagination: line breaking, tables, floats, headers and footers
- A CRDT editing core, built for multiplayer and agent collaboration

And this is what happens on every keystroke:

1. Your input lands in the resident engine as a single WebAssembly call.
2. The engine edits the document and re-measures only the dirty paragraphs.
3. A binary frame delta repaints just the damaged part of the page.

# Architecture at a glance

Where each stage of the pipeline actually runs.

| **Stage** | **What happens** | **Where it runs** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Parse & save** | OOXML in, OOXML out — the parser and serializer round-trip your file byte-faithfully. | Rust (wasm) |
| **Editing core** | Document state, selections, undo, and tracked changes live in a CRDT engine. | Rust (wasm) |
| **Text & layout** | Font shaping, line breaking, and pagination — no browser layout involved. | Rust (wasm) |
| **Rendering** | The engine emits a display list that is replayed onto page canvases. | Canvas + worker |

Table 1. The pipeline — everything before the canvas is native Rust.

## Why it matters

Fidelity needs a real engine. Because layout runs in Rust rather than the DOM, the same code can paint this page in every browser today — and in native apps tomorrow.

BetterOffice is open source and maintained by the OpenOOXML project. Explore the code, file an issue, or just keep typing — everything you see is being computed by Rust, right here in your browser.

BetterOffice is open source and maintained by the OpenOOXML project. Explore the code, file an issue, or just keep typing — everything you see is being computed by Rust, right here in your browser.

items.text: A Rust-native editing engine for DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX. Local-first, collaborative, and entirely yours.
Parse. Edit. Collaborate. Render. All in one resident model.
No conversions. No round-trips. Every edit stays inside the file model.
Every keystroke lands locally first. Peers exchange only updates, then converge on the same file.
